title: Indian Restaurant in West Sussex Joins Michelin Guide Within Six Months of Opening
excerpt: Chef Dayashankar Sharma's BAUJI in Worthing earns a Michelin Guide listing for its Rajasthani-inspired modern Indian menu, adding to the UK's growing recognition of regional Indian cooking.
body:
• BAUJI, a modern Indian restaurant in Worthing, West Sussex, has been selected for the Michelin Guide less than six months after opening in March 2026
  • Chef Dayashankar Sharma draws on childhood recipes from Rajasthan for a menu featuring tandoori avocado, Konkani fish tikka, and dhaba ka murgh
  • Sharma's first restaurant, Heritage in Dulwich, is also Michelin Guide-listed, making BAUJI a notable expansion of Indian fine dining outside London
  • The restaurant has been consistently full since its early weeks, with The Times calling it a standout on England's south coast

A modern Indian restaurant in Worthing, West Sussex, has been added to the Michelin Guide less than six months after opening its doors, marking a rapid rise for chef Dayashankar Sharma's second venture, according to SussexWorld.

BAUJI, which takes its name from the Hindi word for father, opened on Rowlands Road in March 2026. The restaurant draws on Sharma's childhood memories of growing up in Rajasthan, offering a menu that balances regional Indian comfort food with refined technique in a relaxed seaside setting.

From Dulwich to the Seaside

Sharma built his reputation at Heritage, his first restaurant in Dulwich, south London, which earned its own Michelin Guide listing and a loyal following for its contemporary Indian cooking. BAUJI represents a deliberate move toward a more informal atmosphere, trading the capital's intensity for a spot a short stroll from the Worthing seafront.

"Following the success of our Dulwich restaurant, opening BAUJI feels like a natural next step. Worthing's charm, strong sense of community and flourishing independent food scene made it the right location for a more relaxed expression of our cooking."

— Dayashankar Sharma, Executive Chef, BAUJI

The menu includes tandoori avocado and venison, dahi ke kebab wrapped in kataifi pastry, Konkani fish tikka made with stone bass in coconut and curry leaves, and dhaba ka murgh inspired by Rajasthan's roadside eateries. Several Heritage favorites have made the journey south, including shatkora jhinga — prawns flavored with Bangladeshi citrus — and gunpowder broccoli.

Rajasthan on the English Coast

The interior, designed by Sarina Gurung of Cozy Ghar Interiors, uses pink tiles inspired by the sandstone cities of Jaipur. Natural materials including wicker, stone, straw, and greenery create an earthy palette that references Rajasthan without veering into pastiche. Dark, dusty pink banquettes and rattan chairs seat 45 in the main dining room, with an additional 10 covers in a private dining area.

The Times restaurant critic described BAUJI as looking "as if it has been transplanted directly from the poshest folds of Borough Market," noting its clean stone interior and buttermilk curtains. TripAdvisor reviewers have been equally enthusiastic, with visitors praising the quality of the food relative to its pricing and calling the lamb shank curry "absolutely sublime."

Indian Fine Dining Beyond London

BAUJI's Michelin Guide inclusion adds to a growing list of Indian restaurants earning recognition across the United Kingdom. London remains the epicenter, with Gymkhana holding two Michelin stars and the JKS group's Ambassadors Clubhouse earning a new star in the 2026 guide. But the expansion of high-quality Indian dining into smaller coastal towns reflects a broader shift in how British diners approach the cuisine.

For the Indian diaspora in the UK, restaurants like BAUJI serve a dual purpose: they introduce regional cooking traditions to mainstream British audiences while offering a more personal alternative to the generic curry-house format that dominated for decades. Sharma's Rajasthani-rooted menu — with its emphasis on family recipes and roadside eatery traditions — is as much about cultural storytelling as it is about the plate.

The restaurant has been consistently full since its opening weeks. Diners advise booking well in advance. BAUJI is located at 67 Rowlands Road, Worthing, BN11 3NJ.
nri_angle: BAUJI's rapid Michelin Guide recognition reflects the growing mainstream acceptance of regional Indian cuisine in the UK, where diaspora chefs are redefining how Indian food is perceived beyond the traditional curry house.
